topics.label: Lecture framing: initiation and resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students and frames the lecture as a deeper synthesis of previously introduced immune concepts.

topics.label: Innate recognition of danger by PAMPs, DAMPs, and pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain what innate immunity detects, what makes microbial patterns useful signals, and how receptors are encoded and positioned to recognize them.

topics.label: Toll-like receptor recognition and signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how TLRs detect microbial products and how their location and signaling determine the resulting immune response.

topics.label: Non-TLR pattern recognition and inflammatory activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics extend innate recognition beyond TLRs and show how other sensing pathways can drive inflammation and inflammatory disease.

topics.label: Sentinel-cell activation and leukocyte recruitment to inflamed tissue
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how sentinel-cell signals activate local defenses and guide leukocytes from the blood to the site of inflammation.

topics.label: Lymphatic drainage and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how dendritic cells and tissue fluid travel through lymphatic drainage to enable infection screening and adaptive immune activation.

topics.label: Septic shock from excessive systemic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how excessive inflammatory signaling can cause systemic vasodilation, shock, and severe harm.

topics.label: Passive and active resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic distinguishes the removal of inflammatory signals from active mechanisms that instruct the immune system to stop.

topics.label: Tissue repair and persistent inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain what happens to tissue after inflammation, including how it is repaired and how inflammation may persist or be contained when its cause remains.

topics.label: Lecture close: the next lecture on complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic ends the lecture and points students to the subject of the next lecture.
